core_obligations: Preparation (proof lines 11914-11921): sheafification is two applications of the plus construction, the map between the sheafifications is injective, and the identity of the object provides sections of the plus constructions and of the sheafification over the object.

A covering sieve gives an isomorphism (proof lines 11923-11932): the identity of the sieve produces a section of the plus construction over the object restricting to the identity, which provides a morphism from the representable presheaf to the sheafification whose composite with the canonical map is the canonical map, giving the required inverse.

An isomorphism gives a covering sieve (proof lines 11934-11948): a section corresponding to the identity is described by a covering sieve on which the relevant maps come from the sieve, and the transitivity axiom for the topology shows that the sieve itself is a covering sieve.
proof_roadmap: Use the description of sheafification by two plus constructions and injectivity of the resulting map.
From a covering sieve, build the inverse of the sheafified inclusion using the identity section.
From an isomorphism, read off a covering sieve and conclude with the transitivity axiom.
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes covering sieves by the property that the sheafification of the inclusion of the sieve into the representable presheaf is an isomorphism (statement lines 11902-11912). The proof is a complete equivalence: after recording that sheafification is two plus constructions and that the induced map is injective (proof lines 11914-11921), the author shows that for a covering sieve the identity of the sieve produces a section which yields the inverse (proof lines 11923-11932), and conversely that an isomorphism produces a covering sieve whose description is then used with the transitivity axiom to conclude that the sieve itself is covering (proof lines 11934-11948). The non-formal content is the construction of the inverse from the identity section. The claim is H2: two implications with each input named.
